# Proposal: Fractional AI Governance Advisor

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments
**Program:** Fractional AI Governance Advisor, AI Governance Academy
**Basis:** Client Profile Block v1.0 and discovery call notes of 6 October 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. Its headquarters are in the Netherlands, and it operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client has not completed a prior Academy program, so this proposal starts from the Profile Block alone.

The Client's AI portfolio is at an early stage:

* **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
* **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
* **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

The Client describes its AI maturity as Piloting. The regulatory drivers named are the EU AI Act and GDPR. ISO/IEC 42001 is the certification target, with work to start next year. That start date is not fixed and is recorded here as `Unknown`.

An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that there is no inventory of AI systems.

The Profile Block lists two incumbent frameworks: an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and an ISO 9001 quality management system. This proposal does not assume that any specific register, process, control or record exists within them. Whether they can be reused will be confirmed with the Client during Quarter 1.

Your stated objective sets the direction of this engagement: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

## 2. The Case for Continuous Fractional Advisory at Piloting Maturity

At Piloting maturity, governance decisions are made under time pressure. One use case is live, one is approaching production and one is in planning. Each needs a different level of control.

A one-time assessment would describe the current position but would not support the decisions that follow it. Continuous fractional advisory provides senior guidance at each of those decision points. It does so without adding headcount and without displacing the Client's own accountable owners.

The engagement is guided by three principles:

* **Slow AI:** deliberate sequencing rather than rushed deployment.
* **Informed Intent:** decisions made with a clear understanding of risk and purpose.
* **Final Liability rests with the Human:** accountability stays with named people at the Client.

The work draws on three references:

* **GRC Workbook** (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) for governance, risk and compliance structures.
* **Slow AI Kitchen** (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen) for deliberate, practical AI implementation.
* **AI Governance for Boards** (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards) for board-layer reporting, where the Client chooses to use it.

## 3. Annual Arc

Quarters are counted from the engagement start date, which is `Unknown`. The arc is front-loaded so that governance work for visual inspection is completed ahead of the Q2 2027 production timing stated in your objective.

ISO/IEC 42001 readiness work is placed in the second half of the year. If the Client fixes an earlier start date, that work will move forward.

**Quarter 1: Stabilize**

* Establish an AI system inventory in response to the June 2026 internal audit finding.
* Define governance roles and decision rights.
* Open a risk assessment for the visual inspection pilot.
* Prepare questions on the EU AI Act classification of each use case for verification by external counsel.
* Agree with the Client how the German works council consultation constraint applies. Whether and when visual inspection triggers that consultation is `Unknown` and will be confirmed by the Client.

**Quarter 2: Production Readiness**

* Build a pre-production governance gate for visual inspection, covering:
  * human oversight
  * performance monitoring
  * documentation
  * evidence retention
* Review the deployed chatbot against the same criteria.
* Confirm through the inventory where each use case processes data, against the constraint that customer data must stay in the EU.
* Flag GDPR and EU AI Act obligations for counsel verification. They are not presented as settled advice.

**Quarter 3: Assure**

* Prepare an ISO/IEC 42001 readiness gap assessment.
* Recommend a scope for the AI management system.
* Confirm with the Client which elements, if any, of the existing ISMS and quality management system can be extended.
* Agree how the internal audit function is engaged. That engagement is `Unknown` and is subject to the Client's confirmation.

**Quarter 4: Evolve**

* Route the planned sales forecasting use case through the governance intake established earlier in the year.
* Mature the ISO/IEC 42001 readiness work plan.
* Prepare the Month 11 renewal and handover review.

All audit preparation is framed in readiness terms. This engagement does not promise any certification or audit outcome.

## 4. Cadence and Access Model

* **Executive advisory session:** one per month. Participants are to be nominated by the Sponsor.
* **Working session with the governance team:** one per month. Membership is to be confirmed by the Client from the roles listed in the Profile Block.
* **Asynchronous availability:** for defined question categories, with response windows set out in the cadence kit.
* **Quarterly governance review:** one per quarter, measuring progress against the annual plan.

## 5. Scope and Out of Scope

**In scope:**

* governance evolution
* implementation guidance
* audit preparation
* AI strategy
* executive decision support

**Out of scope:**

* legal advice
* certification body functions
* staff augmentation
* incident command

The advisor is not counsel of record. Legal questions, including EU AI Act classification and GDPR interpretation, are routed to external counsel. Regulatory developments raised during the engagement are flagged for counsel verification.

## 6. Price

The program is priced at **US$10,000 per month** over twelve months, renewable. This is a total of US$120,000 for the year.

The Profile Block states a budget approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year. At the program price, that amount covers eight months of the engagement. The Client's fiscal year dates and the funding route for the remaining months are both `Unknown` and are flagged for intake.
